card.name: The word order in 'in order to'
card.fires_on: Mostly the word 'order' right after 'in' in the phrase 'in order to' or 'in order that', in general web prose. It also fires weakly on a few other linking words such as 'of' in 'one of the' and 'a' after 'written by'.

modes.label: In order to
modes.description: The word 'order' after 'in' when it begins a purpose clause.
modes.example: Lord Drayson has fallen on his sword in<< order>> to join the Le Mans race.

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Scattered small words like 'of', 'a' or 'one' inside set phrases, before a descriptive term.
modes.example: Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by<< a>> professional astronomer.

card.writes: It seems to hold back words that mean obviously or clearly, so the next word is not an emphatic adverb.
card.plain: It lights up on the word 'order' in 'in order to', where a purpose clause is about to start.
